Playbook.name: Windows — Pass-the-Hash / Overpass-the-Hash Logon Pattern - SOC Playbook

Metadata.Category: Lateral Movement / Use Alternate Authentication Material

ExecutiveSummary.Overview: A logon (4624) with LogonType 9, LogonProcessName seclogo and AuthenticationPackage Negotiate - the signature runas /netonly leaves when a stolen NTLM hash is used (Pass-the-Hash / Overpass-the-Hash). Triage question: is this an attacker moving laterally with a hash, or a legitimate admin tool that uses alternate credentials?
ExecutiveSummary.BusinessImpact: PtH lets an attacker authenticate as a user without the password, enabling lateral movement and privilege use across the domain.

TelemetryRequirements.Requirement: Windows Security auditing shipped via Elastic Agent to logs-system.security-* (verified live).

Input.name: $username
Input.description: Account used in the alternate-credential logon (TargetUserName).

InitialAssessment.Rule: Some admin tooling and cluster software legitimately uses runas /netonly; the risk is when the account is privileged and the host/timing is unusual.

Investigation.Goal: Determine whether the alternate-credential logon reflects hash reuse for lateral movement or a known administrative tool pattern.

Step.name: Frequency and spread of this PtH signature
Step.Purpose: Isolated on one admin jump host = likely tooling; the same account showing this pattern across multiple hosts = lateral movement.
Step.Query: FROM logs-system.security-* | WHERE event.code == "4624" AND winlog.event_data.LogonType == "9" AND winlog.event_data.LogonProcessName == "seclogo" AND winlog.event_data.AuthenticationPackageName == "Negotiate" AND @timestamp >= NOW() - 4 hours | STATS events = COUNT(*), hosts = COUNT_DISTINCT(host.name), host_list = VALUES(host.name) BY winlog.event_data.TargetUserName | SORT events DESC | LIMIT 25
Step.AnalystNotes: One account, many hosts in a short window = spreading. Confine attention to privileged accounts; a normal user showing this on several servers is high concern.

Step.name: What did the account do on this host after the logon
Step.Purpose: Follow-on privileged actions (special privileges, service creation, share access) turn a suspicious logon into confirmed lateral movement.
Step.Query: FROM logs-system.security-* | WHERE host.name == "$hostname" AND winlog.event_data.TargetUserName == "$username" AND event.code IN ("4672","4673","4688","5140","7045") AND @timestamp >= NOW() - 2 hours | STATS c = COUNT(*), codes = VALUES(event.code) BY winlog.event_data.TargetUserName | LIMIT 10
Step.AnalystNotes: 4672 (special privileges), 5140 (share access), 7045 (service install) after the PtH logon indicate active use of the credential on this host.

Node.Condition: INV-01 shows one account with the PtH signature across MULTIPLE hosts, or INV-02 shows privileged follow-on actions.
Node.Result: True Positive (Lateral Movement via Hash - IR)

Node.Condition: INV-01 shows the signature confined to a known admin jump host / clustering software with an expected account.
Isolated occurrence on one host with no follow-on and account role unclear.

DocumentationChecklist.Item: Attach outputs of INV-01-PTH-SPREAD, INV-02-PTH-FOLLOWON to the case.

FalsePositive.Definition: Legitimate administrative tooling using runas /netonly or clustering software using alternate credentials.

Indicators.Item: Confined to a known admin/jump host or service.
No lateral spread or privileged follow-on.

SOCAction.Item: Confirm the tool/host is expected; close as false_positive; document the benign pattern.

TruePositive.Definition: A stolen hash reused to authenticate and move laterally.

Indicators.Item: Same account, PtH signature across multiple hosts.

SOCAction.Item: Isolate affected hosts; reset the account and revoke sessions.
Hunt the origin of the hash (LSASS access); open IR.

Misconfiguration.Definition: A misconfigured service repeatedly using netonly logons unnecessarily.

Indicators.Item: A service account generating the pattern on its own host by design flaw.

SOCAction.Item: Reconfigure the service to use proper auth; document.

Phase.name: Immediate Actions (0-30 minutes)
Phase.Action: Isolate hosts showing spread; reset $username and revoke sessions.

Phase.name: Containment and Eradication (hours)
Phase.Action: Hunt for LSASS credential theft on the origin; check for tools (mimikatz) and other reused accounts.

Phase.name: Recovery and Hardening (days)
Phase.Action: Enable credential guard; restrict admin logon types; tier admin accounts.

QualityChecks.Check: Signature (type 9 + seclogo + Negotiate) is specific but used by some legit tools - lateral spread and follow-on are the discriminators.
source.ip is often absent for local runas - rely on host spread.

FalsePositiveClosure.Item: Confined to expected admin tooling; no spread or misuse.

TruePositiveClosure.Item: Hosts isolated, account reset, hash-theft origin found, IR closed.
